numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For the Cauchy distribution, `stats.cauchy.pdf(x)` triggers spurious overflow warnings when |x| > 1.34e154 (i.e. sqrt(np.finfo(np.float64).max), and `stats.cauchy.logpdf(x)` returns -inf for |x| > 1.34e154.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: `stats.cauchy.pdf(x)` should not trigger an overflow warning for large |x| (example: x=1e200 gives p==0.0). `stats.cauchy.logpdf(x)` should give correct finite results instead of -inf for |x| > 1.34e154, matching reference values (e.g. x=1e200 -> -922.1787670834676).
trigger_conditions: When evaluating `stats.cauchy.pdf(x)` with |x| > 1.34e154 (threshold stated as i.e. `sqrt(np.finfo(np.float64).max)`).
When evaluating `stats.cauchy.pdf(x)` at x=1e200 (x**2 overflows to infinity and `1/(1 + x**2)` becomes 0; should not trigger a warning), where the test asserts `p == 0.0`.
When evaluating `stats.cauchy.logpdf(x)` at x=1e200, expected finite value `-922.1787670834676` from mpmath-based reference values.

input_output_examples.source: `scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py` `test_pdf_no_overflow_warning`: `p = stats.cauchy.pdf(1e200)` and `assert p == 0.0` (and comment says it should not trigger a warning).

`cauchy._logpdf` was implemented to extend the input range over which `cauchy.logpdf` gives correct results; before the change, `cauchy.logpdf(x)` returned -inf for `|x| > 1.34e154`.
Correctness for `cauchy.pdf` is asserted exactly for `x=1e200`: `assert p == 0.0`, and the test comment specifies the key oracle is that no warning should be triggered.
Correctness for `cauchy.logpdf` is checked against explicit mpmath-computed reference constants in `test_logpdf` (e.g. `x=1e200` -> `-922.1787670834676`).

category_specific_evidence: The discrepancy depends on the magnitude regime: cauchy.pdf(x) overflow/warning behavior changes when |x| > 1.34e154 (i.e. sqrt(np.finfo(np.float64).max)); test coverage includes x=1e200 and expects p == 0.0 without triggering a warning.
The discrepancy for cauchy.logpdf is described as extending the input range over which cauchy.logpdf gives correct results; before the change, cauchy.logpdf(x) returned -inf for |x| > 1.34e154.

A test for cauchy.logpdf uses reference values (computed with mpmath) for x values spanning several magnitude regimes: 0.0, 6e-323, 1e-34, 5e-4, 1.5, 2e18, 1e200, 4e303; refs are -1.1447298858494002, -1.144730135849369, -2.3233848821910463, -85.42408759475494, -922.1787670834676, -1399.283884962481 respectively (as listed in the parametrization).

Implementation notes state the logpdf computation uses formulas intended to avoid overflow: it uses absx = np.abs(x) and discusses avoiding overflow from absx**2 for absx >= np.finfo(x.dtype).max**0.5.
